gen-fs-striper-fs-amulya: Amulya reads contemporary and modern, with curves that keep their gaps generous and never crowd. And Striper hangs a graphic, playful headline above it, which makes the whole page feel comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-striper-fs-plein:
Playful and graphic, Striper leads with a bold plain face.

Plein follows with a clear channel into each round letter, so a longer passage stays reliable and clean, though it is better for brief copy.
gen-fs-striper-fs-spline-sans: Striper's graphic, playful letters have almost no calligraphic shading, so nothing in them steers the eye except shape. Spline Sans does the quieter work, its vertical and horizontal strokes of identical weight suiting a handful of lines.
gen-fs-striper-fs-synonym: Synonym is a clean, dependable sans, drawn as a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings in every curve. But Striper, graphic and playful, is the livelier partner, so this pairing is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-striper-plus-jakarta-sans: Graphic, playful, and plainly built. Plus Jakarta Sans brings tubular strokes like bent copper pipe, modern and precise, though this pairing is better for brief copy than a long passage.
gen-fs-striper-space-grotesk: Chunky, graphic, a bit cheeky. Space Grotesk keeps counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open, but a long passage would tire, as this pairing is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-tanker-archivo: Tanker turns every open curve inward, packing its letters tight with lowercase that looks big beside the capitals. Archivo then opens its curves outward with a commanding x-height, an editorial plain sans that keeps a longer passage approachable though brief copy suits it better.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-asap: Asap is a readable sans whose c forms read as open arcs, with a body height nearly matching the capitals. But Tanker is the one that commands, heavy and tightly spaced, so the pair is good for a handful of lines.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-epilogue: Tanker is heavy and commanding, closing every curve inward with tiny gaps between letters. Epilogue answers with curvy, unclamped monoline letters and stubby ascender tips, an approachable plain sans that makes the contrast the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-fira-sans: Tanker hits hard, with inward-turning curves and tight spacing that make its heavy headlines feel packed and closed. Fira Sans does the opposite job as a plain sans, with wide s curves, no thick-thin contrast and a generous x-height made for short stretches of reading.
